newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt soars as Greenspan fuels bond optimism.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt soars as Greenspan fuels bond optimism.

text.p: Emerging debt prices surged Tuesday, as comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan fueled a powerful rally in U.S. stock and bond markets that spread strength to Brady bonds, dealers said.
In part one of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before Congress, Greenspan said U.S. economic growth was slowing for now and that inflation in 1997 would be quite modest.

The financial markets interepreted his comments to mean the Fed would hold off on raising U.S. rates, and enthusiasm spread rapidly, leading Brady prices to tighten 15-25 basis points across the board.

"It's a resumption of the bull market," said Raul Elizalde, global fixed income strategist at ING Barings. "We're going to continue to test the spread lows and probably go beyond that, probably in the third quarter."
The liquid Brazilian "C" bonds stormed 1-7/8 higher to a bid price of 83-1/4, while Argentine FRBs gained 7/8 to 94-3/4.

Brady bond dealers said the emerging market took its cues from the spectacular moves in U.S. assets. The benchmark U.S. T-bond gained close to two points to yield 6.42 percent, and Dow industrials surgedd 155 points to a record 8062.
The good news of a stable U.S. rate outlook smoothed over any lingering concerns that Asian currency instablity might have a contagious effect on Latin America.

"It's the benign external environment, plus a recovery of confidence that had been shaken last week," one portfolio manager said. "The fear of contagion that had hit everbody has passed, and now people are voting with their wallets."
Prices had risen prior to the start of Greenspan speech, with day traders dominating activity, but the Fed chairman's comments solidified the gains.
